literal: If in spring from the first month or in autumn from the ninth month no commander-in-chief was appointed, only sixty thousand cavalry were sent—they might not penetrate deep, storm cities, or cut timber, but only within three hundred li of the border wear down settlements and forbid planting and raising stock.
idiomatic: In spring from the first month or autumn from the ninth month, if no commander-in-chief was named, only sixty thousand horsemen went—they might not penetrate deep, take walled cities, or fell trees, but within three hundred li of the border they harried settlements and forbade planting and husbandry.

literal: Once the army entered the southern border, infantry and cavalry camps did not follow field paths.
idiomatic: South of the border infantry and cavalry camps did not keep to field paths.

literal: Each of the three routes had one commander leading ten thousand barricade horse scouts each, dispersed in roaming patrols a hundred or ten li out, relieving one another in watch.
idiomatic: Each route had one commander with ten thousand barricade horse scouts, scattered in roaming patrols a hundred or ten li out, relieving one another in observation.

literal: At dusk the horn was the signal and all halted; they ringed the imperial camp from near to far, bending branches into bow-shaped shelters—no stockades, spear lines, moats, or palisades.
idiomatic: At dusk a horn sounded and all encamped, ringing the imperial tent from near to far with bent branches for bow-shaped shelters—no stockades, spear lines, moats, or palisades.

literal: Whenever the army marched, three drum beats—day or night—sent the whole host forward together.
idiomatic: On every march three drum rolls—day or night—sent the whole host forward at once.

literal: Before meeting a great enemy they did not ride war horses; only near the enemy did they mount fresh horses with strength to spare.
idiomatic: Before a great battle they did not ride their war horses; only near the foe did they mount fresh horses still full of vigor.

literal: In formation they did not fight; on retreat they rode.
idiomatic: In the line they held back; on retreat they charged.

literal: They set many ambushes to cut grain routes, lit fires by night, and dragged brush upwind.
idiomatic: They laid many ambushes to sever supply lines, lit fires by night, and dragged brush upwind.

literal: Provisions they carried themselves, scattering and gathering again.
idiomatic: They carried their own provisions, scattering and regathering.

literal: Skilled in battle, able to endure cold.
idiomatic: They fought well and bore the cold.

literal: This is why their troops were strong.
idiomatic: This is why their armies were strong.
